subject.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane

question: Should Active Memory split recall onto per-agent lanes by default, accepting higher concurrent embedded recalls on multi-agent gateways, or should this be gated by an explicit concurrency policy?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but it removes a hidden global throttle in a reply-critical plugin path, and OpenClaw policy treats plugin defaults and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive maintainer choices.

options.title: Require proof, then land per-agent default
options.body: Ask for inspectable redacted multi-agent logs first, then land the narrow per-agent lane fix with release-note context.

options.title: Gate concurrency explicitly
options.body: Pause this PR and route the fix through a config or policy design if maintainers want to preserve a global throttle by default.

options.title: Defer to broader reliability work
options.body: Keep this PR paused until the canonical Active Memory reliability issue settles nonblocking recall, cancellation, and QMD startup together.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then land per-agent default
recommendation.body: Ask for inspectable redacted multi-agent logs first, then land the narrow per-agent lane fix with release-note context.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the strongest recent history owner for the dedicated-lane mitigation that this PR extends.
